prompt: Money in a double is never exact, so convert it to a whole number of cents -- rounding ties away from zero -- and format cents back as a money string.
explanation: Math.round breaks a tie by rounding upward on the number line, so -12.5 becomes -12 rather than -13; rounding the absolute value and re-applying the sign gives the away-from-zero rule that money uses. Once the amount is a long count of cents it is exact, and integer division by 100 gives the dollars while the remainder gives the pennies. String.format("%02d", pennies) pads a single digit with a leading zero so 5 cents prints as .05 instead of .5.
hints: Compute long size = Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 100.0) first, then return -size when amount is negative.
In format, handle the sign separately: remember whether cents was negative, then work with Math.abs(cents).
dollars is cents / 100 and pennies is cents % 100 -- integer division and remainder on a long. Pad pennies with String.format("%02d", pennies).
